Title: Did a quality improvement collaborative make stroke care better? A cluster randomized trial
Author: Power et al.
Comment: The events/totals are the post-intervention patient-level data required for the planned RR synthesis. The reported OR (1.56, 95% CI 1.06–2.31) is not a simple post-intervention arm comparison: it is the cluster-adjusted difference-in-differences interaction effect for change from baseline. Table 3 reports ICC=0.066 for this outcome. No cluster-adjusted post-intervention RR is reported; no RR was calculated or entered.
Design Type: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with interrupted time series and cluster-adjusted difference-in-differences logistic regression
domain: Acute stroke inpatient care implementation/quality improvement
Study Environment: NHS hospitals in the Northwest of England
interaction_type: Hospital participation in a multifaceted quality-improvement collaborative versus normal care
Recruitment source: NHS hospital Trusts in the Northwest of England
Outcome measurement: All-or-none bundle compliance: every one of four early-hours process elements had to be undertaken
outcome_family: in-hospital adherence to evidence-based acute-stroke care
effect_direction: Higher compliance indicates greater adherence; RR > 1 favors the intervention.

Report_ID: Proportion of stroke cases in each hospital treated with tPA
Title: Cluster-Randomized Trial of Thrombolysis Implementation Support in Metropolitan and Regional Australian Stroke Centers: Lessons for Individual and Systems Behavior Change
Author: Levi et al.
Comment: Cluster-randomized trial. The reported adjusted primary effect is an absolute rate difference, not a risk ratio. The postintervention patient-level event counts are unadjusted for clustering, and no ICC is reported in the supplied paper text; per the synthesis plan, an ICC of 0.05 would therefore need to be assumed for a design-effect adjustment if these raw counts are used. No RR was computed here because only verbatim reported numeric values were extracted.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Multicomponent, multidisciplinary tPA implementation-support package') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Topic of Content: Implementation of intravenous thrombolysis for acute stroke
Recruitment source: Stroke cases at participating hospitals identified through the hospital tPA data set and state-level hospital-separation data
Outcome measurement: Number of stroke cases treated with tPA divided by the total number of stroke cases
Outcome variable: Proportion of stroke cases in each hospital treated with tPA
outcome_family: in-hospital adherence to evidence-based acute-stroke care
effect_direction: A higher proportion treated with tPA indicates greater adherence; RR > 1 favors the intervention.

Report_ID: Swallowing screening within 24 h of admission to ASU
Title: Implementation of evidence-based treatment protocols to manage fever, hyperglycaemia, and swallowing dysfunction in acute stroke (QASC): a cluster randomised controlled trial
Author: Middleton et al.
Comment: The paper reports p<0.0001 rather than an exact p value, so p_value is left null under the verbatim-number rule. M_diff=29.2 is the paper's adjusted absolute difference in pre-post change (percentage points), not a simple post-intervention risk difference. No cluster-adjusted RR or OR is reported. For RR synthesis, use the post-intervention patient counts (24/350 control; 242/522 intervention) and account for clustering using the explicitly reported outcome ICC of 0.156; the post-intervention trial profile reports mean cluster sizes of 56 intervention patients and 50 control patients among patients with 90-day data, but no outcome-specific average cluster size is reported for the swallowing-screening denominators.
Design Type: Single-blind cluster randomised controlled trial with pre-intervention and post-intervention patient cohorts
domain: Acute stroke inpatient care; implementation of evidence-based fever, glucose, and swallowing protocols
Study Environment: Acute stroke units in large tertiary referral centres with immediate CT access and on-site high-dependency units
Topic of Content: Implementation of evidence-based acute-stroke care protocols
interaction_type: Multifaceted unit-level implementation intervention versus abridged existing guidelines
Participant type: Adult patients with ischaemic stroke or intracerebral haemorrhage admitted to an acute stroke unit within 48 h of symptom onset
Recruitment source: Participating acute stroke units in New South Wales
Outcome measurement: Presence in the medical record of all three required swallowing-screen elements within 24 h of ASU admission; emergency-department screening excluded
Outcome variable: Swallowing screening within 24 h of admission to ASU
outcome_family: in-hospital adherence to evidence-based acute-stroke care
effect_direction: A higher proportion screened within 24 hours indicates greater adherence; RR > 1 favors the intervention.

domain: Implementation of evidence-based thrombolysis in acute stroke care
